title: Curaçao Jewish Heritage Journey
subtitle: Join Rabbi Joel Sisenwine and TBE congregant and Curaçao native Susan Alvares Correa as we embark on a remarkable journey to Curaçao, a Caribbean island with an extraordinary Jewish heritage, vibrant culture, and breathtaking beauty.
leader: Rabbi Joel Sisenwine & Susan Alvares Correa
pace: Guided touring most days 9:00 AM–3:00 PM, with leisure afternoons
accommodation: Renaissance Wind Creek Curaçao Resort, Willemstad
price_note: Pricing and booking details will be shared once the program is finalized. Registering your interest is not a booking.
intro:
Join Rabbi Joel Sisenwine and TBE congregant and Curaçao native Susan Alvares Correa as we embark on a remarkable journey to Curaçao, a Caribbean island with an extraordinary Jewish heritage, vibrant culture, and breathtaking beauty.

Together, we’ll meet members of today’s Jewish community, explore the people and places that shaped this enduring legacy, share Shabbat and Havdalah, and taste the flavors and traditions that have been passed down through generations. We’ll also venture into Bandabou, rural Curaçao, to encounter Curaçao’s Afro-Curaçaoan history, art, and music, placing the island’s Jewish story within the broader cultural and historical landscape in which it developed.

From the historic Mikvé Israel-Emanuel Synagogue (home to the oldest continuously active Jewish congregation in the Americas), to centuries-old Jewish cemeteries, historic family homes, and the colorful streets of Willemstad, we’ll trace more than 375 years of Jewish life and reflect on a unique Jewish legacy that continues to thrive.
highlights:
Mikvé Israel-Emanuel Synagogue — the Snoa
Beth Haim Blenheim Cemetery
Jewish legacy tour: art, architecture & culture
Kabbalat Shabbat at the Snoa
Afro-Curaçaoan history, identity & art in Bandabou
Open-air Havdalah service with sea view
included:
Five nights at the Renaissance Wind Creek Curaçao Resort, Willemstad
Breakfast daily at the resort
Meals where indicated in the itinerary (welcome dinner, Day 2 lunch, Day 3 lunch and Shabbat dinner, Day 4 gallery dinner, farewell dinner)
All guided touring, entrances, private encounters and transportation as described
not_included:
International airfare (participants book their own flights)
Airport transfers (assistance available on request)
Meals not indicated in the itinerary
Optional excursions on the free day
Travel insurance and gratuities
notes:
Flights: International airfare is not included in the group arrangements. Participants book their own flights, providing maximum flexibility to arrive early, extend their stay, or continue onward after Curaçao.
Travel Assistance: Participants who would like assistance with flights or airport transfers may contact Hannah Berkeley Cohen of L’Dor Vador Travel, who will also serve as a host throughout the journey.
Hotel: The group program is based at the Renaissance Wind Creek Curaçao Resort in Willemstad.
Meals: Breakfast is included daily at the resort. Other meals are included where specifically indicated in the itinerary.
Program Flexibility: The itinerary reflects the planned program. Specific speakers, hosts, cultural figures, and private encounters are subject to availability. Should any featured individual be unavailable during the group’s visit, L’Dor Vador Travel will arrange a suitable and equally compelling alternative whenever possible.
Optional Programming: Additional programming with Rabbi Joel and/or Susan may be offered during periods designated as leisure time and will be communicated to participants on the island.

itinerary.title: Arrival in the Crossroads of the Caribbean
itinerary.subtitle: Arrival Day | Welcome Dinner at 6:15 PM
itinerary.text:
Individual Arrivals in Curaçao
- Participants arrive individually and make their way to the Renaissance Wind Creek Curaçao Resort in Willemstad for check-in.
- Our journey officially begins at the hotel, allowing participants the flexibility to select the flights and travel arrangements that work best for them. Participants are therefore welcome to arrive in Curaçao earlier, extend their stay after the program, or continue onward to another destination.
- For those who would like assistance, Hannah Berkeley Cohen of L'Dor Vador Travel, who will also be accompanying us throughout the journey, will be available to assist participants individually with flight arrangements and airport transfers.
- After check-in, take some time to settle in, relax at the resort, and enjoy your first views of the Caribbean.

Welcome Dinner & Orientation
- This evening, we come together for the first time at Gouverneur Restaurant for our welcome dinner and orientation.
- Meet your fellow travelers and hosts as we introduce the journey ahead and set the stage for our exploration of Curaçao's remarkable Jewish, Caribbean, and multicultural heritage.
itinerary.summary: Participants arrive individually and make their way to the Renaissance Wind Creek Curaçao Resort in Willemstad. Our journey officially begins at the hotel, with flexibility to arrive early or extend your stay. We come together this evening at Gouverneur Restaurant for our welcome dinner and orientation.

itinerary.title: The Sephardic Story of Curaçao
itinerary.subtitle: Touring: 9:00 AM–3:00 PM
itinerary.text:
Breakfast
- Enjoy the breakfast buffet at our resort.

Historic Willemstad
- We begin with a drive through Willemstad, a UNESCO World Heritage city renowned for its distinctive and colorful colonial architecture.

Mikvé Israel-Emanuel Synagogue — The Snoa
- Continue to Mikvé Israel-Emanuel Synagogue, affectionately known as the Snoa.
- Completed in 1732, it is the oldest continuously operating synagogue in the Americas and connects us to a Sephardic Jewish story whose Spanish and Portuguese roots can be traced to the Iberian Peninsula of the 1400s.
- Here, we meet Rabbi Martin Hirsch and enjoy a presentation by Ron Gomes Casseres, a Jewish historian in Curaçao.

Jewish Museum Curaçao
- After sampling kesito, a traditional Curaçaoan Sephardic cookie, we continue into the Jewish Museum Curaçao.
- Explore the museum at your own pace with an audio tour, or choose to join a highlights tour with curator Phyllis Meit.

Lunch at La Vie en Rose
- We enjoy a high-tea-style lunch at La Vie en Rose, in the historic district of Scharloo, known for its elegant colonial mansions, many of which were once owned by prosperous Jewish merchants during the 19th century.

Curaçao's Historic Jewish Cemeteries
- On our way back to the hotel, we pass the newer Jewish cemetery, established in 1864, as well as historic Beth Haim Blenheim Cemetery.
- Established in 1659 by Curaçao's first 12 Jewish families, Beth Haim Blenheim is the oldest Jewish cemetery in the Caribbean. Its richly carved tombstones preserve the story of Curaçao's early Sephardic community and its far-reaching Atlantic connections.

Afternoon & Evening at Leisure
- The remainder of the afternoon and evening is yours to enjoy at leisure.
- Optional programming with Rabbi Joel and/or Susan will be shared once we are all on the island.
- Dinner is on your own this evening; recommendations will be provided.
itinerary.summary: We visit the historic Mikvé Israel-Emanuel Synagogue — the Snoa, completed in 1732 and the oldest continuously operating synagogue in the Americas — followed by the Jewish Museum Curaçao and a private lunch in historic Scharloo. On the way back we pass Curaçao’s historic Jewish cemeteries, including Beth Haim Blenheim, established in 1659.
itinerary.overnight: Renaissance Wind Creek Curaçao Resort, Willemstad

itinerary.title: Jewish Legacies in Art, Architecture & Culture
itinerary.subtitle: Touring: 9:00 AM–3:00 PM | Evening Program: 5:00–8:00 PM
itinerary.text:
Breakfast
- Enjoy the breakfast buffet at our resort.

Art, Heritage & Culture Tour
- Today, we set out on an on-and-off bus exploration of Curaçao's Jewish legacy, art, architecture, and cultural heritage.

Mongui Maduro Historic House
- Visit this meticulously preserved historic plantation house and discover the legacy of the Levy Maduro family, a prominent Sephardic Jewish lineage that significantly influenced Curaçao's economic and social landscape over four generations.

Chobolobo Distillery
- Discover the history and production of Curaçao's iconic Blue Curaçao liqueur, invented by a local Sephardic Jewish family.
- We also sample a crescent-shaped, deep-fried pastry similar to an empanada and commonly found throughout the Dutch Caribbean.

Landhuis Bloemhof & Cathedral of Thorns
- Continue to Landhuis Bloemhof, today a cultural center dedicated to art, heritage, and nature.
- Learn about the history and ideals of the family that has continued to innovate at Bloemhof across generations.
- Visit the extraordinary Cathedral of Thorns, conceived as a space for reflection and healing and as a powerful metaphor for Curaçao's complex history, including colonialism and slavery.

Lunch at Number Ten
- Enjoy lunch together at Number Ten.

Afternoon at Leisure
- Following lunch, we return to our resort for time to rest and enjoy the property.
- Optional programming with Rabbi Joel and/or Susan will be shared once we are all on the island.

Kabbalat Shabbat
- As the sun begins to set, we come together for Kabbalat Shabbat at the Snoa.

Shabbat Dinner
- Following services, return to the resort for an outdoor Shabbat dinner, celebrating the arrival of Shabbat together in Curaçao.
itinerary.summary: We tour Curaçao’s Jewish legacy in art and architecture — the Mongui Maduro Historic House, Chobolobo Distillery, and Landhuis Bloemhof with its Cathedral of Thorns — followed by lunch at Number Ten. As the sun sets we gather for Kabbalat Shabbat at the Snoa, then return to the resort for an outdoor Shabbat dinner.
itinerary.overnight: Renaissance Wind Creek Curaçao Resort, Willemstad

itinerary.title: Afro-Curaçaoan History, Identity & Art
itinerary.subtitle: Bandabou | Day Program: 9:00 AM–4:00 PM | Evening Program from 6:30 PM
itinerary.text:
Breakfast
- Enjoy the breakfast buffet at our resort.

Depart for Bandabou
- Travel west into Bandabou, Curaçao's rural western region, where plantation history, Afro-Curaçaoan traditions, and the island's struggle for freedom remain deeply embedded in the landscape.

Tula Museum at Landhuis Kenepa
- Visit the Tula Museum, housed at the former Kenepa plantation, one of the principal sites associated with Curaçao's great slave revolt of 1795.
- We are personally welcomed by Jeanne Henriquez, historian, activist, and director of the museum.
- Through the story of Tula, leader of the 1795 uprising and today recognized as a national hero of Curaçao, Jeanne introduces us to the history of slavery, resistance, emancipation, and the continuing process of confronting Curaçao's colonial past.
- Our conversation moves beyond history to explore nation-building, national identity, collective memory, and the importance of national heroes.

Santa Cruz
- Continue to Santa Cruz, a secluded beach nestled within one of Bandabou's beautiful natural coves.
- Pit-stop at the legendary home base of Juni "Captain Goodlife" Obersi, one of the island's colorful local personalities and refresh with a cocktail on the shaded terrace overlooking the bay, or enjoy a leisurely stroll along the beach. This short yet relaxed interlude offers an opportunity to experience another side of life in rural Curaçao before continuing our journey.

Art, Rhythm & Curaçaoan Identity: Yubi Kirindongo & Pernell Saturnino
- Continue to the home and atelier of internationally renowned Curaçaoan artist Yubi Kirindongo.
- Known especially for transforming discarded materials into powerful works of art, Kirindongo has developed a distinctive visual language rooted in Curaçao, the African diaspora, social consciousness, and the transformation of what society has cast aside. He personally welcomes us into his world and introduces us to his life, artistic philosophy, and work.
- We are joined by Pernell Saturnino, Grammy Award-winning percussionist and Berklee College of Music alumnus, for an encounter with Curaçao's musical heritage.
- Pernell introduces us to traditional Afro-Curaçaoan rhythms and instruments, including the chapi and tambú, and explores how rhythm, music, resistance, spirituality, and community are intertwined in Curaçaoan culture.
- Drinks and finger food are served during this intimate afternoon gathering.

Return to Hotel
- Return to the resort with time to rest and refresh before our evening program.

Sunset Community Time & Havdalah
- Gather on the resort beach as the sun sets over the Caribbean Sea.
- Share community time followed by Havdalah, marking the transition from Shabbat into the new week.

Art, Books & Dinner in Historic Otrobanda
- Walk together through historic Otrobanda to Sebastopol 9, an art gallery housed in a monumental 18th-century residence that has remained in the same family for approximately three centuries. Today, Philip Chapman and his brothers have given the property a new cultural life as a gallery showcasing emerging Curaçaoan artists.
- Enjoy a private catered dinner buffet inside the gallery, surrounded by contemporary local art.
- During the evening, meet Anneroos Reich, an active member of Curaçao's Jewish community and a board member of the Jewish Museum. Especially for our group she will open her bookstore Hirsch & Reich, outside of opening hours, presenting a curated selection of books relevant to our journey, including Judaica, regional history, literature, art, and culture.
- This encounter also offers an informal opportunity to speak with Anneroos about contemporary Jewish life in Curaçao and everyday island life, connecting the historical Jewish story explored throughout our journey with the community that lives it today.

After Dinner — Evening at Leisure
- Stroll back to the hotel at your own pace, or continue exploring the Otrobanda neighborhood by night.
itinerary.summary: We travel into Bandabou to visit the Tula Museum, meeting historian Jeanne Henriquez, then the home and atelier of artist Yubi Kirindongo with percussionist Pernell Saturnino. We close the day with Havdalah on the resort beach and a private dinner at the Sebastopol 9 gallery in historic Otrobanda.
itinerary.overnight: Renaissance Wind Creek Curaçao Resort, Willemstad

itinerary.title: Curaçao at Your Own Pace
itinerary.subtitle: Day at Leisure | Farewell Dinner in the Evening
itinerary.text:
Breakfast
- Enjoy the breakfast buffet at our resort.

A Day to Explore, Discover or Simply Relax
- Our final full day in Curaçao is intentionally left free of scheduled programming, allowing everyone to experience the island at their own pace.
- Take a self-guided exploratory walk through Willemstad's historic center, or simply relax beside the resort's infinity pool and enjoy its sweeping sea views.
- Those who would like to explore farther afield may choose from a variety of optional excursions and activities. Suggestions will be offered by your hosts.

Farewell Dinner
- On our final night in Curaçao, we come together for a festive open-air farewell dinner at our resort.
- Over dinner, we reflect on the people we have met, the stories we have encountered, and all that we have experienced together during our Caribbean journey.
itinerary.summary: Our final full day is intentionally left free of scheduled programming, so everyone can experience the island at their own pace — Willemstad’s historic center, the infinity pool, or an optional excursion. We close with a festive open-air farewell dinner at the resort.
itinerary.overnight: Renaissance Wind Creek Curaçao Resort, Willemstad

- Enjoy a final breakfast at our resort.

Individual Departures
